nitro carbonyls show an onset threshold while completion remains locally smooth?"}],"feedback_interpretation":"Recent measured outcomes strengthened the case for local, endpoint-specific corrections. Basic and heteroaromatic failures were much larger than the model predicted, including m66 in 49201b5817f204116f7f and m159 in a17bcdddcf0799baeee2. Completion tails also remained highly localized: m178 in 0c5c35afb3a24375c153 and m177 in b514312eda7950cdcf1c had very large V2 underestimates, while lower-ratio cells were much more compact. Donor-containing aromatics were especially geometry-dependent: m205 in 48853fd78c77153b963a and m207 in ec6846c0fcb7df17c97d behaved very differently from compact m206 observations. The m72 and m99 results showed that ratio, sample loading, and plug volume can interact non-smoothly. EA m92 measurements also showed that V1 and V2 move differently across the ratio curve. This batch therefore emphasizes local transition points and matched condition contrasts, while retaining neutral and heavy-atom anchors to constrain generalization.","batch_rationale":"The batch combines failure repair with interpretable local experiments. m11, m66, and m141 sample scaffold-specific nitrogen transitions; m135, m205, m206, and m207 test donor attachment geometry; m72 and m99 probe loading and loading-solvent-volume interactions; and m92 supplies a distinct EA response curve. m177, m178, m159, and several acceptor-rich carbonyls target the high-loss completion-tail and onset regions identified by measured errors. Neutral hydrophobic, halogenated, and ordinary carbonyl controls provide compact calibration anchors across ratios and loading levels. These complementary cells should teach QGeoGNN where condition responses are smooth, where endpoints decouple, and where structural neighborhoods require localized corrections, improving accuracy across both failure regions and the larger ordinary portion of the Row-distribution."}
